title: COF psyche node (RFC 0004, draft for 1.2)
description: elements/psyche/<id>/psyche-node.json — one node of the character's psyche: a value, a belief, a want, a need, a fear, a wound, a stance, a taste, a habit, a contradiction or a rule, in one or two sentences per language, weighted (strength, optional), with its stability, when it appeared (since), a declared risk, the three axes of RFC 0002 and typed links to memories and other nodes, and the people, places and objects it is tied to (RFC 0005). FROZEN for 1.2 (30 October 2026, structure validated on four psyches) — decisions: file name psyche-node.json; one link type `about` (no `toward`); strength optional (tools recommend setting it); stability levels normative, numbers dropped; `risk` field (§ 3 septies); `about: {"user": true}` reserved subject; eleventh kind `rule`. Amended 3 November 2026 by RFC 0005 (before any release): who / where / what lists; links no longer target identities.

gist.description: The node in one or two sentences (100–300 characters per language). Reading rule of RFC 0002 § 3.

strength.description: Weight in decisions (counterpart of a memory's salience). Optional: tools recommend setting it (the builder and cof validate flag a psyche where most nodes leave it unset).

stability.description: What a host may change when it writes the character back (lived nodes, private data): core never; settled only through a lived node that declares it; shifting with evidence (previous value kept in revisions); fragile within one conversation. Levels and rules are normative; no numbers.

risk.description: (§ 3 septies) what this node would make the character do or be, declared by the author or by an AI check and confirmed by the author — `inappropriate` (unsuitable for some audiences or uses: psychological instability, deviant or unhealthy sexuality…), `dangerous` (would make the character harmful if it acted: sociopathy, aggression, manipulation…). Read by builders (purge at build), hosts (refuse or strip at import, by use: an agent with tool or data access never loads a dangerous node) and the file-level tags.content. A declaration, not a detection; criteria are cultural, the field is the hook.

since.description: When the node appeared in the character's life (age and/or date) — places it relative to the memories without making it an event.

false_but_held.description: belief only: the character holds it and the author says it is false (the 'lie').

about.description: stance only: what the stance bears on — a cast identity, a node of any category, or a free label.

who.description: (RFC 0005) The people the node is tied to: a cast identity ('self' or its id) and/or a free name.

where.description: (RFC 0005) The places the node is tied to: an environment variant of the character and/or a free name (geo for a real place).

what.description: (RFC 0005) The objects the node is tied to: a variant that shows the object (an accessory) and/or a free name.

to.description: psyche/<id> or memories/<id>. supports and conflicts target psyche nodes only (checked by the validator). People go in `who` (RFC 0005).

revisions.description: lived nodes only: previous versions of the gist / strength / stability, newest first; keep about ten at most.

user.description: The person interacting with the character (player, user): no identity of the file; hosts read these stances first.

real.description: A real person who is not modelled as an identity.

environment.description: Qualified reference to an environment variant of the same character (appearance/e1, volume3d/env1).

item.description: Qualified reference to a variant of the same character that shows the object (appearance/x1).
